correctness.rationale: A direct symbolic derivative calculation reduces the nonzero stationary points of the positive three-atom Poisson mixture to positive roots of a quartic in x². Four exact primitive integer quartics at rational squared heights and certified sign brackets attain their Descartes bounds, proving every positive root simple and the exact counts 2,1,2,0; the sign of P(0) then determines exactly 3,2,3,1 strict modes. A constructive 249-point equal-weight realization follows from rational masses. Simple critical points and controlled uniform tails prove existence of perturbations to distinct sample sites. check_exact.py reproduces the critical algebra without numerical root finding. No claim is made about all intermediate heights.

originality.rationale: The newly asserted statement is the exact positive real-line Cauchy mixture with rational masses and the 3,2,3,1 mode counts at four specified heights, plus a 249-sample realization, not generic non-Gaussian mode birth. Carreira-Perpiñán (2015) already states generally that Cauchy KDEs can gain modes with bandwidth, so the broad noncausality phenomenon is prior coverage. Its cited Carreira-Perpiñán–Williams (2003) full text discusses general non-Gaussian examples but does not provide the claimed four-height rational witness. The closest indexed equal-weight triple-Poisson result is not the unequal-weight reentrance. No inspected source proves or directly implies the specific four-height exact certificate; priority remains best-knowledge only.
